checked.comment: The vocabulary values match the source: an oblivious adversary picks the finite action sets in the unit ball in advance, the noise is 1-sub-Gaussian, ||theta|| <= 1, and T is known.
The lower-bound setting matches the source. The hard instances use unit-variance Gaussian noise, and the learner is allowed to know T, d and sigma.
Matches Corollary 23: the action sets are infinite, closed and time-varying, and lie in the unit ball.
Theorem 1 is recorded correctly: (log log(nT))^gamma times sqrt(dT log T log n), with gamma taken from Remark 3.
Theorem 2 is recorded correctly: sqrt(dT log n log(T/d)) under the conditions n <= 2^{d/2} and T >= d(log2 n)^{1+eps}.
Theorem 10 is recorded correctly: d sqrt(T log T) when T >= d^5 and n = 2^{d/2}.
Theorem 21 is recorded correctly: d sqrt(eps T log T). Using eps_alg for the paper's eps is an acceptable symbol choice.
Corollary 23 is recorded correctly: Omega(d sqrt(T log T)) for infinite, time-varying action sets.
